paragraphs: I’m a product designer at Meta, working on enterprise products. I’m particularly interested in the intersection of product strategy, interaction design, and technology, and in building functional prototypes to explore new ways of working.

Before Meta, I joined Credo Health as its first designer, helping bring the company from zero to one. I led design for its first mobile and web products, AI-assisted medical document preprocessing, and experiences that made complex patient histories useful at the point of care. I also helped shape the company’s product strategy, commercial narrative, and executive pitch materials.

I was a founding partner of Melostat, a product design and software development studio that was acquired by Credo Health. My work spanned client engagements, design leadership, and business development, including projects for Astellas Pharmaceuticals and Metromile.

At Parachute Health, I led design for new growth initiatives and later helped evolve the underlying platform to support additional product verticals. Much of that work was pixel-agnostic: thinking through reusable application logic alongside engineering and supplier operations.

I spent several years working on Marcel, Publicis Groupe’s internal platform. I joined as a systems designer and eventually became a UX lead and manager. We built tools that connected people and work across the agency network, spanning talent discovery, work sharing, mobility, and timesheets. I partnered with Microsoft’s Fluent Design team on the experience architecture.

One of my favorite earlier projects was Harley-Davidson. I got my motorcycle license so I could ride with local chapters and understand what it meant to ride. Some of the interaction design we did for the ride planner is still among my most satisfying work.
I started my career at West Agile Labs as a QA analyst trying to break products. I went on to build and lead the design and product teams, pitch clients, and work on more than 45 products.

In my free time, I race downhill mountain bikes throughout the northeast corridor, take still images of sunsets when the colors are right, keep a running tab of burgers in New York City and occasionally attempt to make breakfast tacos.
